english.title: Use / possess for trade false / unjust weighing / measuring equipment
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[used]_
(B)_[had in your possession for use]_

for trade

(C)_[weighing]_
(D)_[measuring]_

equipment, namely **(..SPECIFY THE EQUIPMENT..) which was false or unjust
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 17(1) and 84(6) of the Weights and Measures Act 1985.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
used / possessed for use for trade
weighing / measuring equipment which was false / unjust

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 17(1) of the Weights and Measures Act 1985 provides that the equipment shall be liable to be forfeited.
(ii) Section 17(2) of the Weights and Measures Act 1985 provides a defence to this offence.
(iii) Section 83(1) of the Weights and Measures Act 1985 provides that in England and Wales, proceedings for any offence under this Act or any instrument made under this Act. shall not be instituted except by or on behalf of a local weights and measures authority or the chief officer of police for a police area.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
